name: Amphetamine / Adderall
lead: Adderall is a prescription mixed-salts amphetamine product containing roughly equal parts of amphetamine aspartate, amphetamine sulfate, dextroamphetamine saccharate and dextroamphetamine sulfate, approved for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy [2][3]. It is a controlled substance: Schedule II in the US, Schedule I in Canada and Class B in the UK [3].

Its link to appearance runs through appetite. Reduced appetite and weight loss are among its common effects, so some people discuss it as a way to eat less and stay leaner, and looksmax.org members also talk about it for studying, gym sessions and social ease [3][4][5]. The idea follows a chain: less hunger, lower food intake, lower body weight, a leaner face and body. The same stimulant action is the reason it is a controlled drug with a long record of misuse surveys [6][7].

The drug has an unusual history for a stimulant: its ancestor, Obetrol, was a 1960s diet pill, and the product was renamed Adderall and approved for ADHD in 1996 [15][3]. Today it is among the most prescribed medications in the United States, and a nationwide shortage that began in October 2022 made it a news topic well beyond ADHD circles [3]. Research on the drug is dominated by ADHD trials; no published trial has tested it as a weight-loss or appearance treatment in healthy people.

paras: Adderall is approved for ADHD and narcolepsy. Reviews describe long-term stimulant treatment as effective for core ADHD symptoms, with roughly 80 percent of users showing symptom improvement, and a 2025 meta-analysis of 113 randomized trials reported lower all-cause discontinuation for stimulants than for non-stimulants [3]. For narcolepsy, the American Academy of Sleep Medicine's 2021 guideline conditionally recommends dextroamphetamine, with amphetamine considered a third-line option [3].

Reference sources also list non-medical uses: cognitive enhancement, athletic performance, appetite suppression and recreation [3]. They report that low doses can modestly improve cognition in healthy adults while higher doses impair cognitive control, and that stimulants may modestly raise strength and endurance [3]. The NFL, MLB, NBA, NHL and NCAA ban the drug, as do several other sports bodies [3].

Immediate-release tablets act for several hours; Adderall XR capsules last up to about 12 hours in patients aged 6 and over, and Mydayis up to about 16 hours in patients aged 13 and over [3]. A generic Mydayis became available in the US in October 2023 [3].

Reduced appetite and weight loss are common adverse effects, and the FDA advises monitoring height and weight in children and adolescents because of possible reversible growth impairment [3]. This appetite effect is the basis of the appearance interest: eating less produces a lower body weight and, for people with excess body fat, a more defined jaw and face and visible muscle.

The drug's heritage is in weight loss. Obetrol, the amphetamine-salt product from which Adderall descends, was sold as a diet pill in the 1950s and 1960s, and the FDA approved the original formulation, which included methamphetamine, on 19 January 1960 [15]. Following a 1970 FDA order on amphetamine products, the agency withdrew Obetrol's approval in September 1973, citing poorly controlled research that had not tested the individual ingredients [15]. Use specifically for weight loss in healthy people today is off-label, and no dedicated trial has tested it for that purpose.

Amphetamines raise norepinephrine and dopamine signalling, and dextroamphetamine is the more potent central stimulant of the two enantiomers [3]. Oral bioavailability is about 90 percent [3]. A rat study of amphetamine and impulsive decision making examined the dopaminergic and noradrenergic systems involved [14].

Obetrol was made by Obetrol Pharmaceuticals in Brooklyn, New York, and later became a division of Rexar Pharmacal [15]. After the 1973 withdrawal, Rexar removed the methamphetamine components, replaced them with dextroamphetamine and amphetamine, and kept selling the product for years without FDA approval [3][15].

In the 1990s Richwood Pharmaceuticals took over Rexar and promoted the product for ADHD, later adding narcolepsy; the brand name Adderall is described as a contraction of 'A.D.D. for All' [3]. Wikipedia's articles differ on the year of the takeover, 1993 or 1994, and agree that the FDA approved the revised labeling and name in 1996 [3][15]. Shire acquired Richwood in 1997 for 186 million dollars, sold the instant-release name rights to Duramed in 2006, and Teva came to own them through its 2008 acquisition of Barr [3]. The first generic instant-release version arrived in 2002, and a generic extended-release version was permitted from April 2009 [3].

Physical effects include changes in blood pressure and heart rate, insomnia, dry mouth, appetite loss, Raynaud's phenomenon and sexual side effects; large doses can cause rhabdomyolysis, panic attacks and dangerous rises in body temperature [3]. Dose is the main determinant of risk [3]. FDA-commissioned studies in 2011 found no link between therapeutic use and serious cardiovascular events, and a 2022 meta-analysis of nearly four million participants likewise found none, but use is contraindicated in existing cardiovascular disease [3]. Other contraindications include a history of drug abuse, severe agitation or anxiety, moderate to severe hypertension, hyperthyroidism and use alongside MAO inhibitors [3]. Psychological effects include mood swings and anxiety, with psychosis mainly at heavy use [3].

Reference sources describe addiction as unlikely with long-term therapeutic use but a serious risk with heavy recreational use. Recreational doses are far above therapeutic ones, tolerance develops quickly, and in one Cochrane review about 88 percent of chronic heavy users experienced withdrawal lasting three to four weeks [3]. A national survey of 10,904 US college students examined non-medical use of prescription stimulants, and a second survey of 4,580 students examined motives and routes of administration [6][7]. Researchers have also mined Twitter for non-medical Adderall use [10].

Legal status varies widely. Adderall is Schedule II in the United States and Schedule I in Canada; in the UK it is Class B, with up to five years' imprisonment for possession and fourteen for supply; amphetamines are prohibited in Japan and South Korea, and Taiwan and Thailand treat them severely; it sits in Schedule II of the UN Convention on Psychotropic Substances [3].

In October 2022 the FDA first reported a shortage, and news outlets noted in February 2023 that it had lasted over five months [3]. In May 2023 the FDA commissioner said generic drugs are often short because of low profit, that the DEA controls how much is available for prescription, and that prescribing had risen sharply, and the shortage continued into 2025 [3]. A Hacker News thread from 2023 about drug limits blocking Xanax and Adderall access drew 271 comments [16]. For looksmaxxing users the shortage fed the recurring question of access without a prescription.

On looksmax.org, Adderall appears in threads about studying, appetite control, social disinhibition and the gym, including titled threads such as 'adderall is the best social drug', 'adderall makes me more low inhib and nt' and 'anyone here use adderall for the gym' [17][18][19]. Some posts describe prescribed ADHD medication as an appetite suppressant and discuss getting a prescription [4].

Forum threads also ask about obtaining the drug without a prescription. Several replies warn that pills sold this way are often not Adderall; one reply to a first-time user claims such 30 mg pills are usually pressed methamphetamine, and a reply in a UK thread says an unprescribed purchase is probably not Adderall [4][5]. Public health sources do not verify these specific claims, but the posts document a concern the community itself raises.
No studies have tested Adderall for weight loss or appearance goals in healthy people.

ADHD trials are numerous: a 7-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study of mixed amphetamine salts in 27 adults with ADHD [8], a randomized placebo-controlled parallel-group study of Adderall XR in children [9], and a comparison of Ritalin and Adderall in children [11]. Registered trials have also examined mixed amphetamine salts for cocaine dependence and Adderall XR in adult ADHD [12][13].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org Adderall is discussed as a focus drug, appetite suppressant and social enhancer, alongside questions about how to obtain it and warnings about what unprescribed pills contain [4][5][17].

claims.claim: Prescription ADHD stimulants can be used as an appetite suppressant to get leaner.
claims.believers: Forum posters describe using stimulants to cut appetite while studying or training and discuss how to get a prescription [4].
claims.experts: Appetite loss and weight loss are recognised adverse effects, and the FDA advises growth monitoring in children [3]. No trial has tested the drug as a weight-loss therapy in healthy adults, and it is a controlled drug with abuse potential [3][6].

claims.claim: Adderall from an unprescribed source is often really methamphetamine.
claims.believers: Replies to users asking about unprescribed purchases state that common 30 mg pills are pressed methamphetamine [4][5].
claims.experts: Reference sources describe non-medical use patterns among students but do not quantify counterfeit composition [3][6][7].

claims.claim: Adderall is a 'social drug' that lowers inhibition.
claims.believers: Thread titles describe it as 'the best social drug' and as making users 'more low inhib' [17][18].
claims.experts: Reference sources report modest cognitive gains at low doses in healthy adults and impaired cognitive control at higher doses; psychological effects include anxiety and mood swings [3].

claims.believers: Users ask about and describe using it for training sessions [19].
claims.experts: Reference sources report possible small increases in strength and endurance, and the drug is banned by several sports bodies [3].

claims.claim: It helps healthy students focus for school.
claims.believers: Posters describe seeking it to study when they cannot concentrate [4].
claims.experts: Controlled trials are in people with ADHD [8][9]; surveys of US college students document non-medical use for studying and its risks [6][7].

claims.believers: Users ask what amount avoids getting addicted, and others discuss abuse [4].
claims.experts: Reference sources say addiction is unlikely with long-term therapeutic use but a serious risk with heavy recreational use, with withdrawal common in heavy users [3].

card.summary: A controlled stimulant that suppresses appetite as a side effect; nothing tested for weight loss or looks.
card.aka: Adderall, Adderall XR, mixed amphetamine salts
card.note: Schedule II controlled drug with abuse, cardiovascular and psychiatric risks; unprescribed pills may not be what they claim.

quick.overview:
Adderall is a prescription mixed amphetamine product for ADHD and narcolepsy. Reduced appetite and weight loss are common effects, so some looksmaxxing forum users discuss it for appetite control as well as focus.

No trial has tested it for weight loss in healthy people, and it is a tightly controlled drug in most countries.
quick.mechanism: Amphetamines raise dopamine and norepinephrine signalling by promoting release of these neurotransmitters. Dextroamphetamine is the more potent stimulant component of the mixture.
quick.risks: Documented effects include higher heart rate and blood pressure, insomnia, anxiety, psychosis at heavy use, and dependence with withdrawal. It is Schedule II in the US, Class B in the UK and Schedule I in Canada. Forum users themselves warn that unprescribed pills may be other substances.
